item.title: Sly & Robbie’s Sly Dunbar Dead At 73
item.description: Sly Dunbar, the incredibly prolific Jamaican drummer who was one half of the legendary reggae rhythm section and production duo Sly & Robbie, has passed away. According to DancehallMag, Dunbar passed away this morning. Dunbar had reportedly been suffering from health issues for the past decade, though no cause of death has been reported. He was 73. item.description: Pharrell Williams spends a lot of time in Paris these days as the Men's Creative Director for Louis Vuitton, a role he took on in 2023, succeeding the late Virgil Abloh. item.title: Jejune Reunite For Surprise First Show In 27 Years
item.description: Last year, Numero Group reissued music from Jejune, the emo outfit that formed in 1996 and broke up in 2000. Responsible for three albums — Junk, This Afternoon's Malady, R.I.P — the group is back now and ready to shred. Last night they reunited for a surprise show in California, and it was their first in 27 years. The post Jejune Reunite For Surprise First Show In 27 Years appeared first on Stereogum.

item.title: Neil Young Reasserts Amazon Boycott, Gifts Entire Catalog To Greenland
item.description: In October, Neil Young pulled his catalog from Amazon Music and called for a boycott. "BUY LOCAL. BUY DIRECT. BEZOS SUPPORTS THIS GOVERNMENT. IT DOES NOT SUPPORT YOU OR ME," he wrote. Now, he's reasserting that stance on his website and announcing that he's gifting his entire catalog to Greenland amid Trump's threats to seize the territory. item.title: Dope Frontman Takes Issue With Chuck D & John Densmore’s New Project doPE
item.description: Last week, Chuck D and John Densmore announced their debut album no country for old men under the name of doPE. The moniker is meant to combine the beginning of the Doors' lowercase logo and the Public Enemy abbreviation PE, but longstanding NYC industrial crew Dope are pointing out that it will "invite a good bit of market confusion."
